answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism is stake-weighted entry with slow trust accrual: each new agent must post a refundable bond several times larger than one epoch's expected payout, and its voting weight stays near zero until many epochs of peer grading pass. Forging a thousand identities means a thousand real bonds, each slashable if its work goes unattested, so the attacker locks capital far beyond any reward, much as a river needs real volume to move stone. That is the walnut principle: cheap seeds cannot fake a harvest, and clones break long before trust sets like marble.
